mcqs.q: After one half-life, what happens to an individual radioactive nucleus?
options: It has a 50 percent chance of having decayed — radioactive decay is random for any single nucleus.
Every nucleus is guaranteed to have half-decayed after one half-life.
Extension / original length — the same as strain.
The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.

mcqs.q: Is radioactive decay periodic — does each nucleus decay at regular intervals?
options: Yes — half-life is the time between each emission from the source.
The nucleus shrinks to half its original size after one half-life.
No — decay is a random process; half-life is a statistical property of a large population.
Yes — each nucleus 'ticks' at intervals of one half-life until it decays.

mcqs.q: What is the formula for Young's modulus?
options: Extension / original length — the same as strain.
Yes — half-life is the time between each emission from the source.
Force / area — the same as stress itself.
Stress / strain — the ratio in the linear (elastic) region of a stress-strain graph.
